app.notes:
The release candidate for 0.9.5: bug fixes, several boards on one PC, and the board's Settings screen in groups.

### Added

- **Several boards on one PC.** With two or more boards plugged in (any number), the side bar's status line becomes a stack: one row per board with its name, firmware, controller and slot, the one in use marked. Click another row to switch to it; the board then flashes **THIS ONE** on its screen (and blinks its light), so you can see which one you're on. It also flashes when the app connects while several boards are there and before a firmware update. With many boards, three rows show and **N more…** opens a list you can search. The app opens the board you used last. Boards are told apart by their own id (firmware 0.9.5-dev.19), not by the USB serial, which is the paired controller's and can be the same on two boards.

### Changed

- Bundles firmware 0.9.5-dev.19: each board has its own id and an Identify screen (THIS ONE), so the app tells several boards apart; the board's OLED Settings screen opens on a short menu of groups (Haptics/trigger, Audio, Connection, Screen & lights, PC sleep, Reset) with clearer names; settings are checked when the board starts (a damaged save loads the defaults, settings from every earlier release carry over); the controller stays paired when a link drops mid-connect; a cleaner mic start; and fixes for the OLED Diagnostics and Settings screens.
- **A Fail's picked details show in the warning color.** On a game's test sheet, the details you pick under a Fail (Feels weak, Plain vibration only, Sound problems) were green like a pass; they're problems, so they now take the warning color, in every theme and with Color vision.
- **Controller not detected is said once, in Your report.** A game's Setup had its own **Controller not detected** checkbox beside the test sheet's **Controller detected** row, both the same answer. The checkbox is gone: mark **Controller detected** as **Fail** in Your report, and the app still offers to pass the controller to the game as a standard gamepad. A mark you set before shows there as Fail.

### Fixed

- **The same game in two launchers is told apart in the Games list.** A game installed through two launchers (Ghostrunner from Heroic and from Lutris) showed as two identical rows. Each now also says its launcher (Heroic, Lutris, Steam…) in a small label after the name, like Demo or Soundtrack; a long name is shortened first, and the ◆ / ✓ marks keep their place.
- **A save the board drops off during no longer says "All changes saved".** If your board left USB right after Save (unplugged, a loose cable), the bar said everything was saved although the save may never have reached it. Now the bar keeps saying your changes aren't saved, a notice says the board was unplugged, and you can save again once it's back. Restart, BOOTSEL and Reconnect USB still count as done when the board goes away, as they should.
- **Board errors are in your language.** "Your board disconnected", "Your board refused report …", a firmware update's "came back reporting … expected …" and "Normal settings not restored before the slot switch" were shown in English whatever language you use. They now say what happened and what to do in all 7 languages.
- **A failed connect no longer keeps hold of your board.** When connecting failed for any reason other than another program holding the board, the app kept it open, so other programs (or the app's next try) couldn't get it. It now lets go every time. If the board was only slow to answer, the app quietly tries once more before saying anything; a firmware that speaks another protocol is not tried again.
- **The save bar keeps up at once.** After a change or a Save, the bar could take up to a second to switch between "not saved yet" and "All changes saved". It now changes the moment the board confirms.
- **Staged changes survive a reconnect, and never go to the wrong board or slot.** Button assignments, stick curves, calibration and the PC sleep options you hadn't saved yet were lost when the board reconnected, or were compared with the old board's values; a game's button layout going on also threw away the button changes you had staged. Now they're kept when the same board and pairing slot come back (and your button changes come back when the game's layout ends). With another board or another slot they're dropped, a notice says so, and nothing is written there.
- **Back to stable stays on stable.** An update check on the Development channel that answered late, after you went back to stable, could still offer a development build, and automatic updates could install it. Now only the newest check counts, and only for the channel you chose.
- **The tray speaks your language.** Its menu and tooltip were English only and said "DS5 Dongle OLED Edition". They now follow your system's language (all 7) and name your board, for example "Pico 2 W 0.9.5 · Controller connected · Slot 0 · Battery 80%".
- **App settings shows what you changed in the tray.** Unticking Close to tray, Start at login, Start minimized or Check for updates automatically in the tray menu left App settings showing the old switch until you opened the page again. It now follows at once, as it does when the app turns a setting off by itself.
- **One graphics crash no longer turns hardware acceleration off for good.** A single crash of the graphics process (after a driver update, say) switched it off without a word. Now it takes a second crash in the same run, and the app tells you, with **Turn back on**.
- **An update downloaded right after start-up installs (Windows).** If an update downloaded in the app's first 20 seconds, the app's start-up tidy-up could delete it again, and **Restart now** then closed the app without installing anything. The tidy-up now leaves a download alone, and if the file is gone anyway, **Restart now** says so and the app stays open.
- **"No build for this system yet" instead of "Are you online?".** When a new version is out but its build for your system isn't published yet (macOS, usually), Check for updates asked whether you were online. It now says what's really going on, in all 7 languages.
- **The language menu works like every other menu.** In App settings → Language, the arrow keys, Home and End now move through the languages, and Escape closes the menu without closing the settings panel too; the focus goes back to the language button.
- **Share your OLED never replaces a picture without asking.** If you typed a name without ".png" or ".gif", the app added it after the save window had already said yes, and a picture with that name was replaced without a word. Now the save window opens again on the full name, so it asks first.
- **The rail's Keep open says ⌘B on a Mac.** Its tooltip said Ctrl+B on every system; on macOS it now shows ⌘B, the shortcut that works there.
- **The board's chip line is in Portuguese.** The Pico 2 W page said "dual-core" in English; it now says "núcleo duplo".
- **Sony's words in French, Portuguese and Chinese.** Deadzone is now **Zone inerte** (French) and **Zona inativa** (Portuguese), the DualSense Edge's back buttons are **Touches arrière** and Controller mode is **Mode manette** (French), and Chinese calls the controller **控制器** everywhere, as Sony does.
- **Screen readers name a slider's number box in your language.** The box beside each slider was read as "… value" in English in every language.
- **The Development channel window keeps the keyboard.** Escape now closes only that window, not the settings drawer behind it; Tab stays inside the window; and when it closes, the focus is back on **Development**.
- **Escape on the settings drawer puts the focus back on the rail.** In a narrow window, closing the settings drawer with Escape left the keyboard focus nowhere; it now goes to the page's item on the rail, the one that opens the drawer again.
- **Create desktop shortcut says when it fails (Windows).** When Windows refused the shortcut, the tray menu item did nothing you could see. The app's window now opens and says the shortcut couldn't be made, and what to check. All 7 languages.
- **Going back to 0.9.5-dev.17 keeps your game reports.** dev.17 doesn't know the new test sheet and set it aside, and dev.18 no longer wrote the old checklist, so a report was gone after going back. The app now also saves your sheet as the old checklist (as far as it can say it), until 0.9.5 is stable.
- **A game inside gamescope no longer stays "Running" after it closes (Linux).** gamescope's own display helper can stay open after the game ends, and it carries the game's Steam id, so the library kept saying the game was running (and kept its profile on). Only the game's own processes count now.
- **Games inside gamescope see the controller (Linux).** Inside gamescope (the way our HDR setup runs a game, or your own launch options) Steam can't hand its controller to the game, so a game with Steam Input on saw no controller at all, while Games said there was nothing to set up. Games now offers **Turn Steam Input off for** the game, with Undo, when it runs in gamescope or when your report says **Controller detected: Fail** (the report then points to the fix): Proton then passes the DualSense straight to the game. **Turn on HDR** turns Steam Input off with it, and HDR's **Set it up yourself** steps say so. All 7 languages.
- **Each Steam game shows once (Windows).** Windows names Steam's folder in two spellings (`c:/program files (x86)/steam` and `C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam`), and the app took them for two Steam installs, so every Steam game was listed twice, and a profile or rating made on the second tile might never apply. Now it's one Steam, one tile per game. A profile, rating, test sheet or notes you saved on either tile move to the one tile; where both tiles had something, the newer one is kept and nothing is thrown away.
- **No more short freezes while Games looks for Steam (Windows).** The app asked Windows where Steam is installed several times per scan, ▶ Play and Steam restart, and each time the window stopped answering for a moment. It now asks once per scan, in the background.
- **The Games badge tells you what's waiting and takes you there.** The number on the Games rail item said only "1 recommended change", while the library's **Games that need setup** said 0, so there was no way to tell which game to open. Often it isn't a game at all: keeping the controller's volume at full, or a launcher's default Proton, is a change for this computer. Now the badge's tooltip names what's waiting (for example "Recommended: Keep the controller's volume and microphone level at full when it reconnects"; up to three, then "+2 more"). A click on Games opens the settings panel at **Recommended changes**, even when the panel was hidden or you're already on Games. The library counts the two kinds apart: **Games that need setup** counts games, and a new **This computer: 1 change** chip counts the rest and opens them. The two always add up to the badge, and Recommended changes says the same counts in its header (for example "8 games · This computer: 2 changes"). In Recommended changes, each game's changes are listed under its name, then **This computer**. All 7 languages.
- **No more error in the log at every start with Games off.** With Games not allowed, the Controller page's background still asked for game art, was refused and logged an error each time the page loaded. It now asks only once you allow Games, and the art shows as soon as you do, without a restart.
- **You can see which part of the controller drawing has the keyboard focus.** On the standard DualSense, focus, hover and the selected part barely showed on most parts and not at all on Haptic feedback, Speaker, PS, Touch pad and Light bar. Every part of both drawings now gets a clear ring around its own shape, in every colorway and theme, white and black controllers included.
- **A firmware update never writes the wrong board.** With several boards, the update used the first board in update mode it found. It now writes only the board it restarted (by its id, or the one that newly appeared); when it can't tell, it stops and says to unplug the boards you don't want to update. Install on the setup screen and Install again follow the same rule, and the app waits for the updated board to come back instead of switching to another one.
- **Staged changes stay with their own board.** Changes waiting for Save (buttons, calibration, stick curves, PC sleep options) were kept when "the same board" came back, judged by the USB serial; two boards paired to the same controller have the same one. They're now kept only for the same board by its id.
